point: Warm up together for two to three minutes — light jogging, hip openers, and easy two-touch passing before crossing at pace
point: One ball only — after each finish the worker collects it and dribbles it back to the crosser; that jog IS the rest (keep a stack of balls near the crosser to speed resets)
point: Crosser whips the ball off the ground from the byline between the near-post cone and the penalty spot — vary it: rolling toward goal, driven flat, and cut back away from goal across the reps
point: Finisher attacks the cross with a setup touch then a first-time strike — plant foot beside the ball, head still at contact, glance at the target gate before striking
point: Scan first — the finisher looks up at the near/far gate the crosser calls BEFORE the ball arrives, not down at their feet
point: Target: 6 of 10 finishes through the called corner gate within two seconds of the setup touch — count them out loud
point: 5 crosses per set, 4 sets; swap crosser and finisher after each set — collecting the ball is the rest
point: Cushion the setup touch across your body into space; never lunge or reach — land softly after the strike
point: Progression: cross from a deeper, wider position each set and demand one-touch finishes; regression: allow a settling touch and move the gates wider
